target_customer: Fast growing companies that need employee cybersecurity awareness, phishing simulation and security posture tools
problem: Employees are the main entry point for attacks like phishing, and small teams lack an easy way to train and monitor them.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription priced by employee count
product_category: Employee security and security awareness training

founders.name: Benjamin Netter
previous_startups: October, European SME lending platform, ran to 110 employees per his YC bio
founders.background_notes: YC bio: built a Facebook app at 19 that reached 500,000 users in a week and won the Foursquare Global Hackathon at 20. Education not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Phishing simulation templates and training content are standard SaaS; later integrations with Google, Microsoft and Okta add some engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Training and phishing tools were copyable; defensibility rose later with integrations and a security score across systems.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Riot expanded into employee security posture management instead.

market_need_then: In March 2020 TechCrunch reported Riot had signed a handful of clients with plans from 200 USD a month for teams up to 50, as remote work raised phishing exposure.

branding.domain_note: Uses tryriot.com with a try prefix, so the exact riot.com was not used.

identity.mascot_or_character: Albert, a virtual teacher shown in TechCrunch coverage

brand_strength.rationale: A mascot exists in press imagery, but the name collides with Riot Games search results and no brand driven growth is documented.

pivots.why: Company says it is broadening to a full employee security stack

outcome_analysis: Riot grew from a YC W20 phishing training tool into a Paris based employee security platform with 3M seed, 12M Series A and a 30M Series B in 2025 at a reported 170M valuation. Press says the company burned little cash and is doubling revenue, so it looks like a strong early stage success with room to scale.
notes: Series B stated by company blog, SiliconANGLE and SecurityWeek; valuation of 170M reported via TechCrunch per search summary, not opened. Seed 3M and Series A 12M from SecurityWeek search snippet. Competitors: the March 2020 TechCrunch piece names none; KnowBe4 appears only in a later third party comparison, so list is empty by rule. Series B dollar figure also reported as 28.9M EUR.
